analyst.summary: Indus Towers is India's dominant tower infrastructure company, anchored by Bharti Airtel with Vodafone Idea as its second-largest (and highest-risk) customer. FY26 headline profit looked weak only because FY25 profit had been inflated by a one-time receivables write-back; stripped of that, the underlying business grew EBITDA and profit by double digits, added towers/co-locations at a healthy clip, and kept paying a generous dividend. Vodafone Idea's government-granted relief on its AGR dues, plus full clearance of Vodafone Group's security obligations, has reduced (not removed) the main long-standing risk to this stock. At roughly 15x trailing earnings with ~20% return on equity and comfortable debt levels, the stock looks fairly valued for a steady, cash-generative compounder rather than either cheap or expensive -- a Hold.
